subject: general
question: What is the cause of muscle cramps?

options.text: Low glucose level in the blood (hypoglycaemia)
Insufficiency of oxygen supply to muscles
Fatigue and weakness of the body

solution:
The correct answer is __**Insufficiency of oxygen supply to muscles.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Oxygen** is required by muscles to produce energy through** aerobic respiration.**
 
• Inadequate oxygen supply can cause muscle cramps due to the switch to **anaerobic respiration**, which produces **lactic acid** that can lead to cramping.
 
• 
 
Lactic Acid:

 
 
• It is classified as a hydroxy acid and is a carboxylic acid with the chemical formula C₃H₆O₃.
 
• It exists in two optical isomers: L-lactic acid and D-lactic acid.
 
• The accumulation of lactic acid in muscles is often associated with muscle fatigue and soreness, particularly during strenuous exercise.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hypoglycaemia:**

 
 
• **When the amount of glucose in your blood falls below what is considered healthy for you, you have low blood glucose,** also known as hypoglycemia or **low blood sugar.**
 
• This translates to blood glucose levels of less than 70 milligrammes per deciliter (mg/dL) for a large number of diabetics.
 
• **Among the symptoms are restless or shaky, hungry, exhausted, lightheaded, dizzy, or agitated.**
 
• Your heart is racing or palpitating, you're experiencing a headache, and you're having trouble speaking or seeing well.
 
 
 
• **Neuromuscular junctions:**
 
 
• **A skeletal, smooth, or cardiac muscle and the terminal end of a motor nerve form a synaptic connection** known as the neuromuscular junction (NMJ).
 
• It is the** location where the action potential is transferred from the nerve to the muscle.**
 
• It is also the location of many illnesses and the site of action for numerous pharmaceutical products.
